html:
The Senussi order is a Sufi brotherhood founded by the scholar Muhammad ibn Ali al-Senussi, who set up his first lodge in Cyrenaica, eastern Libya, at al-Bayda in 1843.

The order spread a strict but practical Islam among the Bedouin through a network of lodges, which were also schools, markets and rest stops on the desert trade routes to Wadai and the Sahel. It moved its centre deep into the desert to Jaghbub and later Kufra. In effect it became the government of Cyrenaica.

When Italy invaded in 1911, the Senussi led the resistance, and Omar Mukhtar was one of their teachers. The founder's grandson, Idris, became the first king of independent Libya in 1951. Gaddafi's coup of 1969 ended their rule.
sum: The Senussi order is a Sufi brotherhood founded by the scholar Muhammad ibn Ali al-Senussi, who set up his first lodge in Cyrenaica, eastern Libya, at al-Bayda in 1843.
